label: TP
reason: The CodeQL report identifies two paths leading to XSS sinks via string concatenation. Path 1 uses Cookie.getValue() which contains user-supplied data from previous sessions. Path 2 uses Cookie.getName() which also comes from user input. Both variables ('user') are directly concatenated into HTML strings printed to the response writer without any encoding or escaping, allowing attackers to inject malicious scripts.

evidence.note: Sink: response.getWriter().println(...) concatenates user variable containing unencoded cookie data
Flow: Cookie.getName() provides user-controlled input that flows directly into the XSS sink
